questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Many of the people in the villages served by a post office cannot read or write. Write a notice for the notice board of a branch post office, giving the format, the topic and the word limit, to announce that the Gramin Dak Sewak will read out the letters waiting in the letter box and will draft replies for those who cannot read or write. (100 words)

markingPoints.description: Content: the notice clearly says that the Gramin Dak Sewak will read out the letters of the letter box and will draft replies for those who cannot read or write
Format: a capitalised heading, the body of the notice in short clear paragraphs and the designation of the person issuing it at the end
Organisation: the details are arranged in a sensible order, that is, what the camp is, who may come and what the Gramin Dak Sewak will do
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a formal and concise tone suitable for a notice board
Expression: simple sentences and suitable vocabulary that persuade people to come and to ask for help

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
VILLAGE NOTICE BOARD
LETTERS TO BE READ ALOUD

All residents are informed that our Gramin Dak Sewak will sit in the village every morning to read out the letters waiting in the letter box. Anyone who cannot read or write may ask him to read a letter and to write the reply for him. He also carries the dak of the Border Security Force camp that has come here. Villagers have always found him a welcome guest, and a piece of jaggery is all that the village can offer when he brings news of a birth or a wedding. Please tell your neighbours about this camp.

Sd/- The Postmaster

evidence: Everyone feels comfortable asking him to read the
letters and draft the replies.
a piece of jaggery is all that can be offered

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Write an e-mail of about 100 words to a relative of yours living in a city, thanking him for the money orders he sends and telling him how much your family in that arid land depends on them.

markingPoints.description: Content: the e-mail thanks the relative for the money orders and explains that the family survives partly on them, since one crop of bajra cannot feed a family of five
Format: the e-mail layout with a salutation, the body of the message and a closing with the sender's designation
Organisation: the thanks come first and the reason for the dependence follows in a clear order
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, capital letters and a polite tone suitable for writing to an elder
Expression: simple direct sentences that clearly convey gratitude and the need of the family

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Dear Sir,

Thank you for the money order that has reached our branch post office this month. Our Gramin Dak Sewak carried it across the sand dunes and put it into the hands of my mother, and the money has already gone into the food and the medicines that we needed. You must know that in this arid land one crop of bajra in a good year cannot feed a family of five. Akaal or famine is a way of life here, and for each family survival is partly dependent on money orders remitted by a relative. Your gift reaches us when no other service can. Please send one more.

Yours sincerely,
a resident of the Thar

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is holding an assembly to thank the people who carry words to the far-flung villages where no road reaches. Write a speech of about 100 words to be delivered in the assembly.

markingPoints.description: Content: the speech thanks the Gramin Dak Sewaks and gives the hardship of their work, such as the distance walked and the delivery within 24 hours
Format: a speech with a greeting to the audience and a closing line of thanks
Organisation: the greeting comes first, then the example of the work and the closing thanks
Accuracy: correct spelling, punctuation, figures and a formal tone suitable for a school assembly
Expression: clear respectful language that moves the audience and ends with a strong appeal to salute the carriers of words

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Respected Principal, teachers and dear friends,

I stand here to salute the carriers of words. Our Gramin Dak Sewak is the sole postman of a village branch post office in the Thar, and for the last 15 years he has carried the mail to the far-flung hamlets that lie just 2.5 km short of the Indo-Pakistan border. He walks where even bicycles cannot ply, and still the mail is delivered at the border within 24 hours of dispatch from Jodhpur, around 330 km away. Today more than 50 per cent of the total postal workforce is made up of Gramin Dak Sewaks. They are a part and parcel of our social fabric. I salute them all.

Thank you.

just 2.5 km short of the Indo-Pakistan border.
salute to all the people like Khetaram!

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Trace, step by step, the route by which the mail dispatched from Jodhpur reaches the far-flung hamlets that lie 2.5 km short of the Indo-Pakistan border.

markingPoints.description: The mail is dispatched from Jodhpur, around 330 km away from the border
It moves by mail train as far as Barmer, the last railhead
Some 120 km beyond Barmer there is no rail line, so the mail comes off the train onto buses
The buses stop where the road crumbles into sand, 10 km further on and 50 km beyond the last phone
The sand is so soft that even bicycles cannot ply, so Khetaram lifts the bags onto his shoulders and walks
The mail is delivered at the border within 24 hours of dispatch

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1: The mail is dispatched from Jodhpur, around 330 km away from the border.
Step 2: It travels by mail train as far as Barmer, which is the last railhead.
Step 3: Some 120 km beyond Barmer there is no rail line, so the mail is transferred from the mail train onto buses.
Step 4: The buses carry it 10 km beyond the point where the road crumbles into sand, 50 km beyond the last phone.
Step 5: The sand is so soft that even bicycles cannot ply, so Khetaram lifts the bags onto his shoulders and walks over the sand beds and dunes.
Step 6: The mail is delivered at the border within 24 hours of dispatch, because it is his bodily effort that gets it there.

questions.stem: Explain, step by step, why the Gramin Dak Sewak system matters to the people who live in the extremes of India.

markingPoints.description: GDS deliver in interior areas that are often inaccessible by any means besides foot, so they are the sole link with the outside world

They work in rural areas devoid of schools and primary healthcare centres
Through them India Post has reached rural depositors who entrust their monthly savings to the post office
Money orders remitted by a relative decide whether a family in the arid land survives
They form more than 50 per cent of the total workforce, and a proposal to scrap them was rejected
